prs.title: perf(lexer): align `PairLuts` on 128-byte boundary
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf micro-optimization.

`PairLuts`'s size is a multiple of 128. Align it on a multiple of 128, so it occupies the minimum number of paired 64-byte cache lines on x86_64. Once we introduce an aarch64 NEON implementation of `oxc_lexer`, this will also allow ensure `PairLuts` occupies the minimum number of 128-byte cache lines on Apple Silicon machines.

prs.title: perf(lexer): construct `PairLuts` on heap
prs.author: overlookmotel
prs.body:
Perf optimization. This PR completes the refactoring of `PairLuts` from #27189 and previous PRs.

`PairLuts` contains static immutable data. However, it's stored on the heap, because it's too large (~10 KB) to include in the binary as a `static`.

Construct it in a more optimal fashion - allocate space on heap for it first, then write its data in place into that heap allocation. Previously it was constructed on the stack, producing 2 x `memset` calls to zero-initialize the arrays, and 2 full copies of the entire 10 KB data - first between different locations on the stack, and then second from stack to heap. In-place construction avoids all this.

Additionally, make initializing each line of `lutpad` more efficient, removing a `memset` call on each of the 256 lines.

`PairLuts` is only constructed once per process, so it's a one-time cost amortized across all files lexed in that process, but this will improve start-up time a little.

prs.title: perf(linter_codegen): preserve unchanged generated files
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Repeated `cargo lintgen` runs rewrite both linter outputs even when their contents are unchanged. This changes their timestamps and invalidates Cargo's build cache for the linter and its consumers during repeated readiness checks.

Compare the generated bytes before writing, following the AST generator's existing behavior. Changed contents and missing files are still written normally.

Verified that repeated generation preserves both contents and nanosecond timestamps, changing a rule input updates both outputs, and missing outputs are regenerated. `cargo lint-timings` left its snapshot unchanged, and `just ready` passed with 5,060 Rust tests and zero failures using the pinned Node 26.5.0. No generated files, snapshots, or dependencies changed.

AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix(linter/jsx-a11y/lang): validate lang expression strings
prs.author: Pybsama
prs.body:
Fixes #27303

`jsx-a11y/lang` validates `<html lang="foo" />` but accepts the same invalid value in `<html lang={"foo"} />` or a static template.

Apply the existing BCP 47 predicate to known expression strings and expression-free templates. Use cooked template values and unwrap TypeScript/parenthesized wrappers; preserve unknown dynamic expressions and the existing non-string behavior. No new language-tag dependency or broader constant evaluation.

Validation:
- Eight regression cases failed on current main before the fix.
- Both focused lang-rule tests pass, with 20 new regression/control cases including empty/invalid strings, valid languages, dynamic templates, component settings, escaped cooked templates and TypeScript assertions.
- Independent AI code review found no blocking issues; suggested template/wrapper coverage was added.
- Full post-commit `just ready` passed: 98 test targets, 5,061 passed / 161 ignored / 0 failed; formatting, code generation, checks, Clippy and documentation completed with a clean worktree.

AI-assisted with Codex.

prs.title: fix(linter/jsx-a11y/mouse-events-have-key-events): handle nullish event handlers
prs.author: Pybsama
prs.body:
Fixes #27305

`mouse-events-have-key-events` reports absent hover handlers such as `onMouseOver={undefined}` and misses active hover handlers paired with `onFocus={null}`. The same issue affects hover-out/blur and configured handler lists.

Use one local predicate to skip nullish hover values, reject nullish keyboard values, and continue to a later configured active hover handler. Preserve existing component, spread and bare-attribute behavior. Bare attributes retain Oxc's prior behavior, which differs from [the upstream rule](https://github.com/jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y/blob/v6.10.2/src/rules/mouse-events-have-key-events.js).

Validation:
- The new regression test demonstrated five false-positive cases and four false-negative cases before the fix.
- Both focused rule tests pass, with 22 new regression/control cases including default/configured handlers, ordering, dynamic functions, components and bare attributes.
- Independent AI code review found no blocking issues; suggested bare-attribute coverage was added.
- Full post-commit `just ready` passed: 98 test targets, 5,061 passed / 161 ignored / 0 failed; formatting, code generation, checks, Clippy and documentation completed with a clean worktree.

AI-assisted with Codex.

prs.title: fix(linter/jsx-a11y/label-has-associated-control): validate label attribute values
prs.author: Pybsama
prs.body:
Fixes #27301

`label-has-associated-control` accepts empty label and association attributes because its root checks only test their presence. For example, `<label aria-label="" htmlFor="name" />` and `<label htmlFor="">Name</label>` incorrectly pass.

Validate literal attribute values, share the labelling check between the root and descendants, and use JavaScript whitespace rules for label text. Association ids remain untrimmed, matching [the upstream rule](https://github.com/jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y/blob/v6.10.2/src/rules/label-has-associated-control.js). Unknown dynamic values and spreads retain conservative handling.

Validation:
- The new regression test failed on current main before the fix.
- Both focused label-rule tests pass, including 40 new regression/control cases for root/nested attributes, falsy literals, settings aliases, custom label attributes, dynamic values, BOM/NEL whitespace and BigInt values.
- Independent AI code review completed; the Unicode whitespace finding was corrected and retested.
- Full post-commit `just ready` passed: 98 test targets, 5,061 passed / 161 ignored / 0 failed; formatting, code generation, checks, Clippy and documentation completed with a clean worktree.

AI-assisted with Codex.
